note: Data-driven focus areas, role codes, and coordination channels. scripts/coord reads this so the Product Owner can redesign the area set WITHOUT a code change (docs/ORGANISATION.md section 9). If this file is missing or corrupt, coord falls back to its built-in defaults (the same ten areas and sm_owned set) so coordination never breaks. Keep docs/FOCUS_AREAS.md in sync; a change here is a rules change (two peer reviews, or the sole-account self-review).

agent_name.note: A role is a 2-letter area code (below) for a worker, or 'sm' / 'po' for the process roles. <n> is a positive integer, unique per (role, host) and NEVER reused: a replacement worker is a new entity with a new number. Host is lowercase.

channels.sm: Scrum master <-> scrum master handoff (one SM per computer).
channels.po: Product owner <-> product owner handoff (one PO per computer).
channels.takeover: Takeover requests: a live agent asks the fleet to take over an area whose holder has gone quiet.

message.note: Direct agent-to-agent messages, addressed to ONE named agent (refs/coord/msg/<agent>). The generated initial prompt starts a worker; after that, agents talk to each other directly with `coord msg` / `coord inbox` instead of routing through the human. Append-only, like a note; never a lock.

sm_owned_note: Areas the Scrum Master owns and triggers itself. These are project infrastructure, not game content, so the Product Owner never schedules them and `coord next` never routes a plain worker to them: only an agent whose name has role 'sm' is offered them. The SM claims one like any other area when it decides the work is due (docs/ORGANISATION.md section 7).
